purpose: support.js is the generated "dc-runtime" (header says it is built from dc-runtime/src/*.ts with bun). It loads React 18.3.1 UMD from unpkg, turns each .dc.html file (an <x-dc> HTML template with {{ }} bindings plus a `class Component extends DCLogic` script) into a live React class component, and mounts the root file's component into the page. It also lazily fetches and compiles sibling components named by <dc-import>, puts <helmet> content into <head>, turns style-hover/focus/active attributes into generated CSS classes, and provides error boundaries, loading placeholders and editor/streaming bridges for the Claude Design host. It provides no animation, view-transition or motion helpers. All motion in Remi comes from authored CSS and app code. Production must replace the runtime with compiled TSX that keeps the rendering semantics listed below.
layout:
DOM STRUCTURE THE RUNTIME PRODUCES (production must copy it or deliberately account for it): 1) Before React loads, the runtime injects `` so the raw template never shows. 2) On boot, is replaced by `

The template's top-level nodes are children of that wrapper. 3) If the root file's data-props has NO `$preview` key (true for Remi.dc.html, Remi Home, Foundations and Textbook; false for Roll), the runtime appends FULL_PAGE_CSS: `html,body{height:100%;margin:0}#dc-root,#dc-root>.sc-host{height:100%}`. 4) EVERY renders its OWN wrapper `

Everything else is dropped. So Remi's `` and `` get an absolutely positioned, full-size wrapper. The other screens (Today, Timeline, Calendar, Projects, Workspace, Routines, Transition) get a normal-flow block wrapper, so `height:100%` inside them resolves against an auto-height div. The 1920x1080 and 2560x1440 targets are handled in Remi.dc.html's renderVals (for context): - The `frame` prop selects W×H: 1920×1080 (default), 2560×1440, or 'Fit window' (W×H = window.innerWidth×innerHeight). - Scale is sc = 1 for 'Fit window', otherwise min(vw/W, vh/H). - The frame is centred: x = round((vw − W·sc)/2), y = round((vh − H·sc)/2). - The app root `[data-screen-label="Remi app"]` is absolutely positioned at left:x, top:y, with width W, height H, transform:scale(sc) and transform-origin:0 0. - It sits inside a `position:fixed; inset:0; overflow:hidden; background:color-mix(in oklch, var(--ink) 6%, var(--paper))` letterbox. - The app root is a grid with `grid-template-columns:88px minmax(0,1fr)` (nav rail plus main). Main is a grid with `grid-template-rows:72px minmax(0,1fr)` (header plus a main area of absolutely stacked sections). - A resize listener updates vw and vh. components.description: 1) `{{ path }}` in text -> `{fmt(path)}`. fmt rules: - undefined -> render nothing (the runtime also logs a console.warn once per component+expression: `[dc-runtime] : {{ expr }} never resolved — rendered as empty`). - null or boolean -> nothing. - React element or array -> rendered as-is inside a Fragment. Remi Textbook's `{{ b.math }}` uses this with a React.createElement('div', {dangerouslySetInnerHTML}). - Anything else -> String(v), so 0 renders '0' and NaN renders 'NaN'. - Literal text around interpolations is emitted as plain strings. A text node with no {{ }} is returned verbatim, including its newlines and indentation. - A whitespace-only text node is DROPPED only if it contains no U+0020 space (for example pure '\n' or tabs). Otherwise it is kept, so the browser renders a collapsed space between inline siblings. JSX strips this whitespace, so add {' '} where inline elements were separated by indented newlines. 2) Attribute whose whole value is one binding, `attr="{{ path }}"` -> `attr={path}` with the raw JS value (function, object, number, boolean, ref). 3) Mixed attribute `attr="a {{ x }} b"` -> template string, with null/undefined becoming ''. 4) Literal attribute -> string. 5) `style="k:v; k2:{{ e }}px"`: interpolate the string first, then convert it to an object with cssToObj: - kebab-case property names become camelCase; `-webkit-x` becomes `WebkitX`. - `--custom` properties keep their name. - All values stay strings, so no px is auto-appended. - An empty value (an undefined binding) becomes '' and React removes that property. 6) `class` -> className; `for` -> htmlFor. 7) camelCase attributes written in the template (onClick, onMouseEnter, readOnly, tabIndex, srcDoc, etc.) are preserved exactly. components.name: Helmet manager (<helmet> -> document.head)
components.description:
`<helmet>` is renamed to `<sc-helmet>` before parsing, and the compiled builder returns null during render. Each render walks the helmet's children:
- SCRIPT: appended once, deduplicated by src or textContent.
- LINK and META: cloned once, deduplicated by href, src or outerHTML. A stylesheet link can be replaced by an inline <style> from a bundled blob (window.__resources and __resourceBlobs).
- Any other tag (STYLE, TITLE): a 'live' element keyed by `componentName|childIndex`. It is created once in head, and its attributes and textContent are patched when they change.
Nothing is ever removed on unmount, and there is NO interpolation inside helmet. If the helmet has the attribute data-dc-atomics, the runtime also injects ATOMIC_CSS utility classes. No file in this project uses that, so the atomics are unused.
Helmets exist only in Remi.dc.html, Remi Home, Remi Foundations and Remi Textbook. The child screens (Today, Timeline and the rest) have none and depend on Remi.dc.html's global :root tokens and keyframes.
Production: move the tags to index.html (viewport meta, title 'Remi', Google Fonts preconnect and stylesheets) and the <style> blocks to global.css.

components.name: Pseudo-class sheet (style-hover / style-focus / style-active)
components.description:
A single <style> is appended to head when first needed. For each unique (pseudo, css) pair it creates class `scp<base36 counter>` and inserts the rule `.scpN:hover{decl !important;decl !important}`. For `before`/`after` the rule is `.scpN::before{css}` without !important. The class is appended to the element's className.
Because of !important, hover and focus styles OVERRIDE inline styles, and the inline `transition` still animates them.
Usage counts: style-hover 74, style-focus 16, style-active 3.
Hover patterns that set custom properties: `--sh:1` (Textbook section rows reveal children via `var(--sh, 0)`), `--hov:1`, and `--row:1` combined with a background.
Production: CSS classes or modules with `:hover{… !important}`, or move the base styles out of inline style so specificity works.

components.name: x-import / external module loader (UNUSED in Remi)
components.description: `<x-import from="url.js|.jsx|.tsx" component="Name">` or `component-from-global-scope="Name"`. It fetches the module (Babel-transforms jsx/tsx with presets react+typescript), evaluates it with new Function(React, module, exports, require), and resolves the component from module.exports[name], a newly added window function global, window[name], or module.default. It also supports custom elements (tags whose name contains '-') and dotted global paths, polling every 50ms up to 30000ms. There is also deck-stage slide keying through data-om-slide-id, an 8-char hex id. No Remi file uses x-import or deck-stage.

dataConsumed: Template source: the innerHTML of <x-dc>. Boot also re-fetches location.href and uses the raw text between `<x-dc…>` and the LAST `</x-dc>`, so camelCase attributes survive the HTML parser.

Logic source: the textContent of `script[type=text/x-dc][data-dc-script]`. It must define `class Component extends DCLogic`. The script body runs as `new Function('DCLogic','StreamableLogic','React', src + ';return Component')`. Top-level consts and functions are module-scoped, evaluated ONCE per file and shared by all instances (for example Remi's `const STORE='remi.v1'` and `SAVED = loadSaved()`, and Roll's constants shared by 13 instances). `React` (UMD 18.3.1) is in scope.

data-props (on the script tag): a JSON map propName -> {editor:'text'|'enum'|'color'|'boolean', default, options?, tsType, section?}, plus an optional `$preview:{width,height}`. Keys starting with '$' are stripped from props meta. Only the ROOT receives the defaults as props.

Remi.dc.html data-props: frame enum ['1920 × 1080','2560 × 1440','Fit window'], default '1920 × 1080', section Viewport; motion enum ['Full','Reduced'], default 'Full', section Motion; accents color pairs, options [['#526e2a','#47619c'],['#00737e','#5e5a9a'],['#1f744f','#32669a'],['#884b75','#007187']], default ['#526e2a','#47619c'], tsType string[], section 'Brand stand-ins'; serif boolean default true, section 'Brand stand-ins'.
Roll.dc.html data-props: value text, default 'Wed 2 Dec', tsType string; $preview {width:240, height:64}. The default applies only when Roll is viewed standalone.
Template scope (vals) = {...userProps, ...logic.renderVals()}. renderVals keys WIN over same-named props. Props are directly addressable in templates.
sc-for scope additions: the `as` name (default 'item') and `$index` (used once: Remi Textbook `data-row="{{ $index }}"`).

dc-import props used in this project: Remi passes `model="{{ model }}"` to Today, Notes, Timeline, Calendar, Projects, Workspace, Routines, Transition and CheckIn. CheckIn also gets open, pid, session, prefill, onClose (from on-close) and onSave (from on-save). Roll gets `value` (a string such as 'Wed 2 Dec' or '+3.5') in Projects, Foundations, Home, Timeline, Today and Workspace.

componentDidUpdate(prevProps) receives the RAW host prevProps: user props plus __name, __hintSize, __tplId, __hostStyle and key. CheckIn uses `componentDidUpdate(prev){ if (prev.session !== this.props.session) this.reset(); }`.
window.React / window.ReactDOM, loaded from unpkg unless already present.
window.__resources (a URL -> replacement-URL map used for offline/export bundles) and window.__resourceBlobs (URL -> Blob).
document.documentElement.dataset.theme or the ?theme=dark query param (canvas background only).
document.body[data-dc-editor-on] (shows unresolved {{ }} as visible monospace chips).
`<meta name="design_doc_mode" content="canvas">` in the root template enables canvas mode. Not present in this project.
interactions: EVENT BINDING: `onX="{{ handler }}"` passes the function returned from renderVals straight to React, so handlers receive React 18 SyntheticEvents.
Semantics to preserve: onChange fires on every keystroke for inputs and textareas. onMouseEnter and onMouseLeave do not bubble. onFocus and onBlur bubble (React uses focusin and focusout).

Events used in this project (count): onClick 121, onMouseEnter 28, onChange 27, onMouseLeave 26, onKeyDown 24, onBlur 17, onMouseMove 5, onFocus 3, onDragStart/onDragOver/onDragEnd/onDrop 2 each, onDragEnter/onDragLeave 1, onPointerDown/Move/Up/Cancel 2 each, onDoubleClick 1, onMouseDown 1.

EVENT_MAP (lowercase -> React): onclick, onchange, oninput, onsubmit, onkeydown, onkeyup, onkeypress, onmousedown, onmouseup, onmouseenter, onmouseleave, onfocus, onblur, ondoubleclick, oncontextmenu, onmousemove, onmouseover, onmouseout, all onpointer* events (down/up/move/enter/leave/cancel/over/out), ongotpointercapture, onlostpointercapture, ontouchstart/end/move/cancel, ondragstart, ondragend, ondragenter, ondragleave, ondragover, onanimationstart, onanimationend, onanimationiteration, ontransitionend. Any other on* attribute becomes 'on' + uppercase third character + the rest (so onDrop and onScroll work).

Hover, focus and pressed states come from generated classes with !important, never from JS. Examples: `style-hover="background:color-mix(in oklch, var(--ink) 4%, transparent)"` (19 uses), `style-focus="background:var(--paper-raised); box-shadow:inset 0 0 0 1px var(--hairline)"` (12 uses), `style-active="transform:scale(0.98)"` (3 uses, on primary buttons such as 'Tell Remi').

Hover-driven CSS variables: `style-hover="--sh:1"` on draggable Textbook section rows, which children read as `var(--sh, 0)` to reveal controls. Also `--hov:1` and `--row:1`. Production must use the same parent-hover custom-property technique, or `.row:hover .child`.

Refs: `ref="{{ fooRef }}"` works because the value is passed as React's ref. The logic uses them for focus (for example Remi's palette input `setTimeout(() => palRef.current.focus(), 30)`), measurement and scroll.
The runtime has no keyboard handling. ⌘K/Ctrl+K and Escape are handled in Remi's own logic through window keydown listeners added in componentDidMount.

Editor-only postMessage bridge:
- Posts `{type:'__dc_booted', rootName, propsMeta, preview}` to window.parent after boot or a props update.
- Posts `{type:'__dc_design_mode', mode}`.
- Listens for `__dc_theme` {theme:'light'|'dark'} and `__dc_probe`.
Production does not need any of it.
The Remi Textbook drag-and-drop relies on `draggable="{{ sec.draggable }}"` passing a boolean or string attribute straight through.
motion: The runtime provides NO animation helpers, spring engine, view-transition wrapper, enter/exit animation or motion flag. All motion comes from inline `transition:` strings in templates, @keyframes in Remi.dc.html's <helmet><style>, and app code that calls document.startViewTransition directly. Production must port these as written.

Stable DOM identity is what makes the CSS transitions work. Keys are positional: template child index, and sc-for item index. So when renderVals output changes, the SAME DOM node is kept, its inline style changes, and the declared transition animates from the old computed value.

Key example: Roll.dc.html digit columns. Each part is a vertical strip of cells, moved by `transform: translateY(-i*1.25em)` with `transition: transform var(--dur-slow) var(--spring-soft)`, inside a 1.25em-high overflow:hidden window. The strips are keyed by index, so the node persists and the digits roll. Production must keep index keys, or keys stable per position, for Roll parts and cells. Otherwise the roll animation is lost.

Elements that mount directly in their final state do not transition. Remi therefore keeps all 8 screen <section>s mounted and cross-fades them with opacity and visibility instead of mounting and unmounting. The runtime has no enter animation other than authored keyframes.

setState merges into this.state synchronously and schedules one batched React re-render (React 18 createRoot automatic batching). Several setState calls in one handler therefore produce a single commit and a single transition start.

Motion tokens defined in Remi.dc.html's helmet (global, not part of the runtime; reference for porting):
- --dur-fast:140ms; --dur-base:240ms; --dur-slow:440ms
- --ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)
- --spring-soft: linear(0, 0.049 5%, 0.156 10%, 0.283 15%, 0.408 20%, 0.522 25%, 0.62 30%, 0.702 35%, 0.769 40%, 0.864 50%, 0.922 60%, 0.956 70%, 0.976 80%, 0.987 90%, 1)

Reduced motion (Remi.dc.html, not the runtime): `:root[data-motion="reduced"]{--spring-soft: steps(1, jump-start)}` and `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){:root{--spring-soft: steps(1, jump-start)}}`. applyTweaks() sets document.documentElement.dataset.motion to 'reduced' or 'full' from the `motion` prop, and reduced() also checks matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').

View transitions (Remi.dc.html plus Projects and Workspace):
- Rules: `::view-transition-group(remi-goal){animation-duration:420ms;animation-timing-function:cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1)}`; `::view-transition-old(remi-goal),::view-transition-new(remi-goal){height:100%;width:auto;object-fit:none;object-position:left top}`; `::view-transition-old(root),::view-transition-new(root){animation-duration:220ms}`; `:root[data-motion="reduced"]::view-transition-group(*){animation-duration:0s}`.
- Names: the Projects card gets `view-transition-name:{{ r.vt }}` ('remi-goal' when vtPhase==='from' and vtId matches, else 'none'). The Workspace goal gets `view-transition-name:{{ vtGoal }}` ('remi-goal' when vtPhase==='to').
- Sequence: setState({vtPhase:'from', vtId}), then in the callback call startViewTransition(() => new Promise(res => setState({screen:'workspace', ws:id, vtPhase:'to', instant:true}, res))), then on finished call setState({vtPhase:null, vtId:null, instant:false}).
- The runtime's setState callback firing after commit is what makes this sequence work. Production must resolve the promise after the DOM commit (flushSync, or a callback or useLayoutEffect).

Other Remi keyframes (global): `remi-pulse` 0%{box-shadow:0 0 0 0 color-mix(in oklch, var(--overload) 50%, transparent)} 100%{box-shadow:0 0 0 7px color-mix(in oklch, var(--overload) 0%, transparent)}; `remi-settle` from{opacity:0;transform:translateY(6px)} to{opacity:1;transform:none}; `remi-tick` 0%{transform:scale(0.6)} 60%{transform:scale(1.08)} 100%{transform:scale(1)}.

Editor-only streaming shimmer (not for production): `@keyframes sc-shine{0%{background-position:100% 50%}100%{background-position:0% 50%}}`. It applies to .sc-placeholder and .sc-interp.sc-missing under html.sc-dc-streaming, with a ::before gradient `linear-gradient(90deg,rgba(217,119,87,0) 25%,rgba(247,225,211,.95) 37%,rgba(217,119,87,0) 63%)`, background-size 400% 100%, `animation: sc-shine 1.4s ease infinite`. Only the first 8 animate; from the 9th on (`:nth-child(n+9 of …)`) it is static at color-mix 8%.

Print: `*,*::before,*::after{animation-delay:-99s!important;animation-duration:.001s!important;animation-iteration-count:1!important;animation-fill-mode:both!important;animation-play-state:running!important;transition-duration:0s!important}`, so every animation shows its end state when printed.
algorithms:
EXPRESSION RESOLVER resolve(vals, src), used for every {{ }} and every sc-for list or sc-if value. Steps in order:
1) Trim; an empty expression -> undefined.
2) If the whole expression is wrapped in one pair of parentheses (parensWrapWhole: the depth never returns to 0 before the last char), recurse on the inside.
3) findTopLevelEquality: scan left to right tracking depth for [ ( and ] ). At depth 0, the first '=' or '!' followed by '=' (not preceded by '=' or '!', and with non-empty text before it) gives the operator: '===' or '!==' if the next char is '=', else '==' or '!='. Resolve both sides recursively and compare with the matching JS operator. Quotes are not tracked, so '==' inside a string literal breaks this.
4) A leading '!' -> !resolve(rest).
5) Literals: 'true', 'false', 'null', 'undefined'; numbers matching /^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$/; strings wrapped in matching ' or " quotes, with no escape processing.
6) Path: an IDENT /^[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*/ looked up in vals, then any sequence of `.IDENT`, `.digits`, or `[expr]` (bracket contents resolved recursively as an expression, with nested brackets depth-tracked). Traversal is null-safe (a null/undefined intermediate gives undefined). Any other character gives undefined.
There is NO arithmetic, ternary, && or ||, < >, or function call. Unsupported syntax silently yields undefined.

ATTRIBUTE COMPILER compileAttr(raw):
- If raw matches /^\s*\{\{([\s\S]+?)\}\}\s*$/ -> returns resolve(vals, inner), preserving the raw type.
- Else if raw contains '{{' -> split on /\{\{([\s\S]+?)\}\}/g, odd parts resolved with `?? ''`, then joined into a string.
- Else -> the constant string.

cssToObj(css): for each piece of css.split(';'), a naive split that is not paren- or quote-aware, find the first ':'. prop = the text before it, trimmed; if prop starts with '--' keep it, else kebabToCamel (replace /-([a-z])/g with the uppercase letter, so '-webkit-font-smoothing' -> 'WebkitFontSmoothing'). value = the text after it, trimmed. It is applied only when a DOM element's evaluated `style` is a string. An object style would pass through, but no template binds a whole-style object.

collectProps(node, kind):
- Skip 'sc-name' and 'data-dc-tpl'.
- Decode 'sc-camel-kebab-name' -> camelName.
- 'hint-size' -> captured and dropped.
- 'style-<pseudo>' -> pseudoClass(pseudo, value) and dropped.
- For kind dc-import or x-import: names containing '-' -> camelCase. x-import keeps aria-* and data-* as they are.
- For kind dom: class -> className, for -> htmlFor, names starting 'on' -> EVENT_MAP[name] || 'on' + name[2].toUpperCase() + name.slice(3).

encodeCase(html), a pre-parse text transform:
1) Expand self-closing `<dc-import …/>` and `<x-import …/>` into open and close tags.
2) `<helmet>` -> `<sc-helmet>`.
3) camelCase attribute names matching /(\s)([a-z]+[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*)(\s*=)/g -> ` sc-camel-<kebab>=`. For example onClick -> sc-camel-on-click, which decodes back to onClick.
4) select, table, tbody, thead, tfoot, tr, td, th and caption tags -> sc-raw-<tag>, so the HTML parser does not foster-parent them around sc-for/sc-if. They are unwrapped back to real tags at render.
The template is then parsed via `<template>.innerHTML`, so the browser's HTML parser normalises invalid nesting.

Keying:
- Top-level and child builders get key = their positional index j.
- An element's key = `${index}` + (for elements whose descendants are ALL inline text tags — a abbr b bdi bdo br cite code del dfn em i ins kbd mark q s samp small span strike strong sub sup u var wbr — excluding script, style, textarea, option, title, select, canvas, iframe, video and audio) `|` + contentKey.
- contentKey = clone the element, strip all attributes from its descendants, take innerHTML s, compute h=5381 and for each char h = ((h<<5)+h+charCode)|0, and return `${s.length}.${(h>>>0).toString(36)}`. It is static at runtime and only matters for editor hot-reload remounts.
- sc-for: an outer Fragment key = position, each item Fragment key = item index, and children key = j.
- A template attribute `key` overrides all of this.

hostPositionStyle(style): parse the dc-import `style` (a string through cssToObj, or an object), keep only the keys whose kebab form is in {position, left, right, top, bottom, inset, width, height, z-index, transform}, and return undefined if none remain. It is applied as the child's sc-host wrapper style.
hint-size parsing: 'W,H' split on ','. Placeholder uses width W and height H, defaulting to '100%,60px'. While the child's template is streaming, the host also gets min-width W and min-height H.

importantify(css) for pseudo-class rules:
1) stripComments, which is quote-aware and leaves unquoted url(...) intact.
2) Split declarations on ';' at paren depth 0 outside quotes (skipping unquoted url()).
3) Trim, drop empties, and append ' !important' unless the declaration already ends with !important.
4) Join with ';'.
The rule is `.scp<n>:<pseudo>{…}`, or for before/after `.scp<n>::<pseudo>{css}` with no !important. Class names are 'scp' + base-36 counter, cached per `${pseudo}|${css}`, and inserted with sheet.insertRule at the end of one lazily created <style> in head.

walkText rendering: see the text rules in the translation cheat-sheet. While streaming, undefined shows a `.sc-interp.sc-missing` chip; with body[data-dc-editor-on] it shows `.sc-interp.sc-unresolved` with the text '{{ expr }}'. Otherwise it renders nothing and calls console.warn once per (component, expr).

walkFor: list = compileAttr(list)(vals). A non-array renders [] (warning if it was not null/undefined). While streaming, a missing list renders Array(hint-placeholder-count) of undefined. Scope for item i = {...vals, [as || 'item']: item, $index: i}.
walkIf: v = compileAttr(value)(vals). If v is undefined while streaming and hint-placeholder-val is present, use that instead. Render the children if v is truthy.

walkComponent (dc-import):
- name = the `name` or `component` attribute (both are removed from the attribute list).
- The style attribute is removed and compiled separately.
- props = {key, __hintSize, __tplId, __hostStyle: hostPositionStyle(style), ...each propGetter}.
- A propGetter named 'dcProps' is spread with Object.assign if it evaluates to an object.
- Children, if any, become props.children.
- Renders h(getDC(name), props).

walkElement (DOM):
- props = {key, 'data-dc-tpl': tplId, ...each propGetter}.
- If style evaluates to a string it goes through cssToObj.
- value or checked that is undefined becomes '' or false.
- Pseudo classes are appended to className: [className, ...scp classes].filter(Boolean).join(' ').
- sc-raw-* tag names are unwrapped to real tags.

DCLogic (StreamableLogic) contract:
- constructor(props): this.props = props || {}; this.state = {}. Subclass class fields such as `state = {...}` or `palRef = React.createRef()` run after super, so they can read this.props.
- setState(update, cb): if __host exists, patch = typeof update === 'function' ? update(this.state) : update, then this.state = {...prev, ...patch} SYNCHRONOUSLY. It then calls host.setState(s => ({__v: s.__v + 1}), cb). A null patch still re-renders. Calling setState inside the constructor is a no-op because __host is not set yet.
- forceUpdate() delegates to host.forceUpdate().
- componentDidMount(), componentDidUpdate(prevProps) and componentWillUnmount() default to no-ops.
- renderVals() returns {} by default, and its result is merged over props.
- logic.props is refreshed before every renderVals call and again in componentDidUpdate.
- All lifecycle calls are wrapped in try/catch with console.error, so errors never unmount the page.
- When a class is hot-swapped: the old instance's componentWillUnmount runs, the new instance gets state = {...newInitial, ...oldState}, and componentDidMount fires after the next commit, provided the template is present and there is no error.
- A logic class that fails to construct is replaced by the base StreamableLogic (template rendered with props only). The (class, registry.ver, shallowEqual props) triple is remembered so construction is not retried on every render.

Lifecycle ordering difference: the root's logic is ready at construct time. Children, however, are fetched asynchronously. On first mount a child renders a placeholder with base logic, so the parent's componentDidMount runs BEFORE the children's real logic exists. When the child's HTML and JS arrive (updateHtml and updateJs both bump the registry and forceUpdate), the host reconciles to the real class and calls its componentDidMount on that update's commit.

ensureFetched(name): runs once per name. url = './' + encodeURIComponent(name) + '.dc.html'. window.__resources[url] may redirect it, and a bundled blob is used if one exists; otherwise fetch(url). A non-OK response logs '[dc-runtime] sibling fetch for "X" failed: … — the reference renders as an empty placeholder.' The response is parsed with parseDcText, which uses the raw text slice between the first `<x-dc…>` and the last `</x-dc>`, plus the DOMParser-parsed script and data-props. It then sets propsMeta and preview, calls updateHtml if html is empty, and calls updateJs if Logic is empty.

updateHtml(name, html): store html. If this is the root, detect design_doc_mode. compileTemplate, stamping data-dc-tpl indices depth-first over elements. registry.bump, which increments ver and calls every subscriber.

updateJs(name, src): uses a sequence guard. evalDcLogic(src). If the result is not a function, sets logicError '<name>.dc.html: <script data-dc-script> must define `class Component extends DCLogic`'. On throw, sets logicError '<name>: msg'. Then bump.

boot():
1) parseDcDocument(document).
2) rootName comes from location.pathname: decoded, last path segment, with .dc.html or .html stripped (for example 'Remi', 'Remi Home'). If the path is not a .dc.html it falls back to baseURI.
3) markFetched, then adoptParsed (props meta, template, JS).
4) If window.__resources is absent, re-fetch location.href to recover the raw template text.
5) Replace <x-dc> with div#dc-root, add FULL_PAGE_CSS if there is no $preview, and createRoot().render(StandaloneRoot).
Startup order: hideRawTemplate(); loadReactUmd() (sequential async=false script tags with SRI); init(): prepend BASE_CSS to head, expose the window API and set window.__dcContentKeyed = true, then boot now if the DOM is ready, else on DOMContentLoaded.
createStreamTracker(staleMs = 60000): records a streaming start time per name and ignores viewportKey 'dc-model'. live(name) is true if the entry is newer than 60 s. Editor-only.

Remi-level frame scaling, the algorithm the runtime leaves to the app (for the 1920/2560 targets): [W,H] = frame==='2560 × 1440' ? [2560,1440] : frame==='Fit window' ? [vw,vh] : [1920,1080]; sc = Fit ? 1 : min(vw/W, vh/H); x = round((vw − W·sc)/2); y = round((vh − H·sc)/2). The app root is placed absolutely at (x,y) with size W×H, scale(sc), and transform-origin 0 0.
backendImplications: The runtime makes no backend or API calls. Its only network use is loading React/ReactDOM (and Babel, unused here) from unpkg, re-fetching the page's own URL, and fetching sibling ./<Name>.dc.html files. Production should replace all of this with a bundled React + TypeScript build (Vite): TSX components imported statically, React from npm, no runtime template compilation, and NO `new Function` eval. The eval would violate a strict CSP, which a Ninety One corporate deployment is likely to enforce.

The `model` object built in Remi.dc.html's renderVals and passed to every screen through `model="{{ model }}"` is the frontend/backend contract. Its data (projects, tasks, feed, funds, routines, doneOn, bauDone, notes) and its actions become API-backed repositories, services and endpoints. Examples of actions: updateProject, logChange, createProject, removeProject, updateRoutine, addRoutine, removeRoutine, toggleTask, toggleBau, addNote, updateNote, removeNote, setAllFunds, saveCheckIn, openRoutine, previewDay. In the prototype all of this is DCLogic state plus localStorage: key 'remi.v1', debounced 250ms in componentDidUpdate; Remi Textbook uses 'remi.textbook.v1'.

The root 'tweak' props from data-props (frame, motion, accents, serif) are Claude Design editor controls. In production, motion (Full/Reduced) and possibly the accents/serif brand choices become user preferences, persisted locally or server-side. frame is a design-review viewport simulator and should be dev-only.

Fonts load through <helmet> from Google Fonts: Albert Sans ital,wght 0,300..700 and 1,400..600; JetBrains Mono 400 and 500; Libre Caslon Text ital,wght 0,400, 0,700 and 1,400; Material Symbols Outlined opsz,wght,FILL,GRAD 20..24,300,0..1,0, with icon_names add, arrow_forward, calendar_month, check, chevron_left, chevron_right, close, edit_note, north_east, notes, repeat, search, stacks, today, unfold_more, view_timeline and display=block. Production should self-host these (corporate network, privacy, CSP) or at least declare them in index.html.

Error isolation: the runtime gives each DC instance its own error boundary, and all lifecycle errors are logged, never thrown. Production should wrap each screen and the drawer in an ErrorBoundary so one failing screen does not blank the app.
risksAndQuirks: BUG in the prototype: Workspace.dc.html line 233 has `style-hover="background:{{ d.hov }}"` on the date-picker day buttons. style-* values are NOT interpolated, so the generated rule `.scpN:hover{background:{{ d.hov }} !important}` holds an invalid declaration that the browser drops. The day cells therefore have NO hover background in the prototype. The intent was probably hover = d.hov: 'var(--ink)' for the selected day, else 'color-mix(in oklch, var(--ink) 6%, transparent)'. Decide whether to implement that.

There is no <sc-else>. It would be treated as an unknown element and its children would always render. Templates use complementary flags (isHome/notHome, empty/noX) instead. Keep that pattern or use a ternary in TSX.

The expression language is tiny and fails silently: unsupported syntax gives undefined and renders empty. All logic lives in renderVals. When porting, keep derivation in the component body, hooks or selectors.

Each {{ }} text interpolation is wrapped in <span class="sc-interp">. This changes flex and grid item counts (gap applies between literal text and the value) and :nth-child counting. For pixel fidelity, wrap interpolations in spans, or check each flex container that mixes text and bindings.
Whitespace-only text nodes that contain a space character are rendered, which gives inter-element spaces in inline contexts. JSX drops them. Add {' '} where needed.

Every component instance adds a wrapper `div.sc-host` in normal flow. Percentage heights inside child screens resolve against this auto-height div unless the dc-import passes position/inset/width/height through `style`. Only Notes and CheckIn do (position:absolute; inset:0). Non-positional properties in a dc-import style are silently DROPPED.
Only the ROOT receives the data-props defaults. Child components get only the props passed explicitly. Roll's default value 'Wed 2 Dec' is preview-only.

setState is synchronous here: this.state updates immediately and updater functions see the already-merged state. React's class setState and hooks are asynchronous. Audit any read of this.state after setState in the same handler (none found that depend on the new value). Watch instance fields computed during render and read in handlers (Remi's `_palFlat` and `_palSel`): use refs in hooks.
componentDidUpdate(prevProps) receives raw host props, including internal __name, __hintSize, __tplId and __hostStyle. There is no prevState argument. Lifecycle exceptions are swallowed.

There is no memoisation anywhere. Every root setState rebuilds `model` and re-renders ALL screens (all 8 sections stay mounted) plus the drawer and palette. Production can optimise, but it must keep the cross-fade behaviour of always-mounted screens, which also preserves each screen's local state.

sc-for uses INDEX keys. DOM nodes and child component state are reused by position when lists reorder, insert or remove items: focused textareas can 'move', and child DC state follows the position, not the item. Transitions such as the Roll digit strips rely on this. If production switches to id keys, re-verify that the transitions still fire.
Remi Textbook overrides the key on its chart iframe with `key="{{ b.fkey }}"` to force a remount and reload of srcDoc. Replicate it with key={b.fkey}.

<helmet> injects global CSS and tags into head during render and never removes them. Styles are not scoped per component. Child screens depend on Remi's :root tokens and keyframes, and Remi Home, Foundations and Textbook each have their own helmet with their own token copies. Production needs one shared global token stylesheet.

style-hover, style-focus and style-active rules use !important to beat inline styles. A production CSS port that keeps inline styles must also use !important, or move the base styles into classes. style-focus maps to :focus, so it also shows on mouse click, not only :focus-visible.
cssToObj splits on every ';' with no paren or quote awareness, so values containing ';' (data: URIs) would break. None exist in the current templates.
The camelCase-attribute regex runs over the ENTIRE template text, including text content and helmet CSS. Any `fooBar =` sequence gets rewritten. This is cosmetic and not triggered in this project.

The template is parsed by the browser HTML parser, so invalid nesting (a div inside a p, a button inside a button, an a inside an a) was auto-corrected in the prototype DOM. Translate from the parsed structure, not the raw text, where nesting is invalid.

Boolean attributes written with no value (for example bare `draggable`, `disabled`) evaluate to '', which React treats as false for true boolean attributes. Current usages: `draggable="{{ sec.draggable }}"`, `draggable="true"`, `readOnly="{{ locked }}"`, `tabIndex="-1"`.

Opening the .dc.html files over file:// breaks the sibling fetches: child screens stay as grey placeholders. The prototype must be served over http, which matters when reviewing screenshots against a local file.

Editor-only features to DROP in production:
- data-dc-tpl and data-sc-name attributes
- hint-size, hint-placeholder-count and hint-placeholder-val
- streaming states and the sc-shine shimmer
- canvas mode (#f0eee6 / #2e2c26 backgrounds)
- the postMessage bridges
- the window globals (__dcUpdate, __dcStreaming, __dcSetProps, __dcRootName, __dcAnnotatedTemplate, __dcTemplateSource, __dcBoot, __dcRegistry, getDC, DCLogic, StreamableLogic, __dcContentKeyed)
- x-import, deck-stage and ATOMIC_CSS (all unused)

Keep in production:
- `data-screen-label` attributes are app-level. Remi's goHome uses document.querySelector('[data-screen-label="Remi app"]') to fade out (opacity 180ms var(--ease-out)) before navigating to 'Remi%20Home.dc.html'.
- The multi-page navigation between the .dc.html pages (Remi, Remi Home, Textbook, Foundations) should become client-side routes.

React 18.3.1 production UMD, with no StrictMode, so effects are not double-invoked. If production enables StrictMode, every logic that adds window listeners in componentDidMount must clean up symmetrically (Remi already removes its resize and keydown listeners).
actionsInvoked: DCLogic.setState(update: object | (prev) => object | null, cb?): synchronous shallow merge into logic.state, then a batched re-render of that component's subtree; cb fires after commit.
DCLogic.forceUpdate(): re-renders the host (Remi Textbook calls it 4 times).
registry.bump(name) / bumpAll(): increments ver and notifies subscribers (Dispatcher, StandaloneRoot, StreamableComponent.__sub, which clears __err and calls forceUpdate).
window.__dcUpdate(name, kind 'html'|'js'|'props', content, streaming?, viewportKey?): editor streaming entry point that updates the template, logic or props meta.
window.__dcSetProps(name, overrides): editor tweak-panel prop overrides for the root. This is how frame, motion, accents and serif change in Claude Design.
Helmet: appends <script>, <link>, <meta>, <style> and <title> to document.head, and sets documentElement data-dc-canvas in canvas mode.
Pseudo sheet: sheet.insertRule(`.scpN:pseudo{...}`) in a runtime <style>.
externalCalls: https://unpkg.com/react@18.3.1/umd/react.production.min.js, integrity sha384-DGyLxAyjq0f9SPpVevD6IgztCFlnMF6oW/XQGmfe+IsZ8TqEiDrcHkMLKI6fiB/Z, crossOrigin anonymous, async=false. Skipped if window.React and window.ReactDOM already exist, and replaceable through window.__resources[url].

https://unpkg.com/@babel/standalone@7.29.0/babel.min.js, integrity sha384-m08KidiNqLdpJqLq95G/LEi8Qvjl/xUYll3QILypMoQ65QorJ9Lvtp2RXYGBFj1y. Loaded only for x-import of .jsx or .tsx, so unused in Remi.
fetch(location.href) on boot, to recover the raw root template text. Skipped when window.__resources exists; errors are ignored.
fetch('./' + encodeURIComponent(Name) + '.dc.html') once per imported component name: Today, Notes, Timeline, Calendar, Projects, Workspace, Routines, Transition, CheckIn, Roll.

window.parent.postMessage({type:'__dc_booted', rootName, propsMeta, preview}, '*') and {type:'__dc_design_mode', mode}, only when the page is inside an iframe. It listens for message types '__dc_theme' and '__dc_probe'.
Google Fonts stylesheets and preconnects come from the Remi helmet (declared in Remi.dc.html; the runtime only clones those <link> tags into head).
localState: StreamableComponent.state = {__v: number (render counter bumped by every logic setState), __err: string|null (set by getDerivedStateFromError)}.

StreamableComponent instance fields:
- logic (the DCLogic instance)
- __name
- __needsDidMount (true after a hot swap)
- __streamingNow and __htmlStreamingNow (render-time snapshot)
- __failedLogic, __failedUserProps, __failedVer, __ctorError (constructor-failure memo)
DCLogic instance: props, state (author-defined), __host (back-pointer), plus any author instance fields (refs, timers such as Remi's saveT, fT and mT, and memo fields such as _palFlat and _palSel).

Registry entry per component name: {html, tpl (compiled render fn with __annotated), Logic, jsStreaming, htmlStreaming, ver, subs: Set<fn>, fetched, propsMeta?, preview?, propOverrides?, logicError?, jsSeq?}.
Helmet manager: mounted Set (dedup keys such as 'SCRIPT|src', 'LINK|href', '__dc-atomics'), live Map ('<name>|<i>' -> head element), designDocMode, canvasStyleEl, appTheme.
Pseudo sheet: a cache Map ('pseudo|css' -> class name) and a counter n.
External modules: cache, pending, reportedMissing, polling, babelLoading.
warnedHoles Set: deduplicates 'never resolved' warnings per component and expression.
StandaloneRoot and Dispatcher: a useState tick used to re-render on registry bumps.
persistence: The runtime persists nothing and never touches localStorage.

App-level persistence (outside this file, for reference): Remi.dc.html uses the localStorage key 'remi.v1' with shape {projects, tasks, feed, funds, routines, doneOn, bauDone, notes, m2:true}. It is saved 250ms after a change in any of those state slices, detected by reference comparison in componentDidUpdate. It is loaded once at script evaluation through a top-level `SAVED = loadSaved()`, which requires Array.isArray(s.projects). resetData removes the key. Remi Textbook uses 'remi.textbook.v1'.
copyText:
Runtime console and overlay messages (developer-facing, not product copy):
- 'circular import: A → B → A'
- '[dc-runtime] <Name>: {{ expr }} never resolved — rendered as empty'
- 'sc-for list="…" is not an array (type)'
- '<Name>.renderVals(): <msg>'
- '<Name>.dc.html: <script data-dc-script> must define `class Component extends DCLogic`'
- '[dc-runtime] sibling fetch for "X" failed: <url> returned <status> — the reference renders as an empty placeholder.'
- '… has no <x-dc> block — not a Design Component.'
- 'x-import `from` cannot contain {{ … }} — module URLs are resolved at parse time; use a literal URL'
- '[dc] failed to load React or boot:'
The Remi helmet sets the document title to 'Remi'.
sampleData:
The runtime has no seed data. The only data it interprets is the data-props JSON on each logic script tag:
- Roll.dc.html: {"$preview":{"width":240,"height":64},"value":{"editor":"text","default":"Wed 2 Dec","tsType":"string"}}
- Remi.dc.html: {"frame":{"editor":"enum","options":["1920 × 1080","2560 × 1440","Fit window"],"default":"1920 × 1080","tsType":"string","section":"Viewport"},"motion":{"editor":"enum","options":["Full","Reduced"],"default":"Full","tsType":"string","section":"Motion"},"accents":{"editor":"color","options":[["#526e2a","#47619c"],["#00737e","#5e5a9a"],["#1f744f","#32669a"],["#884b75","#007187"]],"default":["#526e2a","#47619c"],"tsType":"string[]","section":"Brand stand-ins"},"serif":{"editor":"boolean","default":true,"tsType":"boolean","section":"Brand stand-ins"}}
Remi's applyTweaks maps these props onto the page:
- accents[0] -> --pc-accent and accents[1] -> --fi-accent, set on documentElement.style. When absent they fall back to the helmet defaults oklch(0.5 0.1 128) and oklch(0.5 0.1 265).
- serif === false -> --font-display: var(--font-ui).
- motion -> documentElement data-motion 'reduced' or 'full'.
ATOMIC_CSS (unused, since no helmet has data-dc-atomics) defines: .fx, .col, .grid, .ac, .jc, .jb, .f1, .noshrink, .wrap, .fw5–.fw8, .fs11–.fs16, .fs20, .fs22, .upper, .tc, .nowrap, .gap8/10/12/16/24, .m0, .mt8/12/16, .mb8/12/16, .posrel, .posabs, .round, .ohide, .bbox, .pointer, .w100, .b0.
